title: Retire the macOS AI workstation: lima sandbox, darwin agent stack, and mini as thin host

statements.text: The lima sandbox subsystem is permanently removed from dotfiles-ai: sandbox-vm, sandbox.json, the lima/ instance templates, the atuin-workspace LaunchAgent and loader, sandbox data keys (atuin_workspace, lima_home, build_workspace, workspaces), sandbox shell aliases, and LIMA_SANDBOX.md.

The mac-mini stops applying the dotfiles-ai workstation stack: all darwin LaunchAgents (dbsctr-embedding, dbsctr-code-embedding, dbsctr-knowledge-reconcile, dbsctr-reranker, dbsctr-spawner, dbsctr-watchdog, pm-postgres-backup, history-projection-refresh, herdr-server, atuin-workspace) and their loaders are deleted from the source, and the mini's dotfiles-ai config is retired so nothing re-renders them.

The Try Omarchy VM is the verified replacement host: atuin runs as the self-hosted fleet server (podman quadlet, 18.24.8, fleet-syncing) and PM/DBSCTR PostgreSQL runs as the pm-postgres quadlet (pgvector 19beta3, healthy). Verified live on the VM during discovery.

The herdr desktop binary and its installed state on the mini are NOT removed in this initiative; only its declarative plumbing and auto-start configuration retire. Binary removal is operator-gated on completed migration and explicitly deferred.

The VM's pm-postgres quadlet has no backup timer today; the darwin backup agent retires without a linux replacement. Accepted risk with follow-up slice; the pm-kernel refactor proceeding in a parallel operator session owns the eventual design and this initiative must not touch pm-kernel internals.

The DBSCTR knowledge store (DKS) is dialed down to documented-dormant: experimental, not developed further; its spec documents current state and the darwin delivery retirement. DKS plan artifacts remain as historical record. Future work refactors rather than resumes the darwin design.

On the VM, knowledge services (embedding, reranker, reconcile) run on demand inside DBSCTR cycles against pm-postgres; the darwin daemons were the macOS workaround, so deleting them is behavior-neutral on the VM.

Continuous validation is a new experimental feature still to be developed — not retired here. Only the obsolete lima-backed execution path from its prototype (local_engine.py + engine/lima.yaml) is removed with the lima subsystem; the feature's VM-native development (dagger backend against the local podman socket) proceeds as the operator's separate follow-on effort.

Verified survivors with live linux consumers must not be removed: state-root-exec (hermes, codex, herdr-host scripts; active on the VM), install-dbsctr-embedding (OS-neutral installer), enable-pm-postgres (linux quadlet path), enable-atuin-server (linux), the remote-* install scripts (fleet remote user environments), the herdr-host build path, and dagger_backend._local_engine (local socket/container engine validation, unrelated to lima).

Personal dotfiles drop the stale residue: LIMA_HOME/COLIMA_HOME/COLIMA_CACHE_HOME exports in common_profile, the '# Added by Colima' ssh-config include, and the /Volumes/ext/state/lima Spotlight exclusion path.

The mini teardown is this initiative's deployment step: boot out and remove all dotfiles-ai LaunchAgents including the drift obsidian agents (never repo-managed), remove the plists from disk, retire ~/.config/dotfiles-ai/chezmoi.toml, and leave the machine applying only the personal dotfiles.
Post-merge convergence: the shared ext working tree fast-forwards to main, the VM applies clean (no removed targets remain managed), and the mini has no loaded dotfiles-ai agents.

dotfiles-ai is a public repository: deletions must not expose secrets, private hosts, or credentials in diffs or docs. Publication checks run before push against the repository's existing public-content authority.
No scope over MGM/company-VM work, colima on pi400, blackarch bundles, or any new feature work; this initiative only deletes and documents.
No pm-kernel or pm-postgres schema changes; the parallel pm-kernel refactor session owns that surface (see INT-005).

The obsidian LaunchAgents found running on the mini (server, watcher, source-pulls) are drift: they exist on disk but are not managed by the current source, so no repo apply can remove them; teardown removes them explicitly.

The lima instance data, LIMA_HOME state root, and LaunchAgent were already torn down on the mini during discovery (instance deleted, /Volumes/ext/state/lima removed, agent booted out and disabled, plist removed); the source changes make that state permanent instead of re-creatable at next apply.
